base_rating.description:
The rating for the base case: its loadings (the "before" figures)

buses.description:
Take out each bus: every branch and DC line connected to it, which
cuts off its loads, generators and shunts.

elements.description:
Ids to take out, one at a time. A bus id (bus:101) takes out the
bus, and ids joined by "&" (line:1:2:1&line:2:3:1) go out together.
When absent, every in-service branch, generator and/or bus, as
chosen below.

limit_pct.description:
Loading, as a percent of the rating, above which a branch is
overloaded.

lists.description:
Run the contingencies of this lists file (`.stnl`): its
`contingency` records and `contingency_set` rules. Equipment the
case lacks is reported in the summary's notes and skipped. Takes
the place of `elements`, `branches`, `generators`, `buses` and
`pairs`; `planning` is unused.

lists_text.description:
Lists text (`.stnl`) to run in place of a `lists` file, as the
setup builds it from its subsystems. Wins over `lists`.

monitors.description:
Check only what the `monitor` records of this lists file (`.stnl`)
name: branch flows and bus voltages with their own limits, and
interfaces. Every rated branch and every bus when absent.

monitors_text.description:
Lists text (`.stnl`) whose monitor records choose what is checked,
in place of a `monitors` file. Wins over `monitors`.

pairs.description:
N-2: take the chosen branches and generators out two at a time,
every pair once, instead of one at a time. Buses stay one at a time.

planning.description:
Run these NERC TPL-001 planning events instead of every branch and
generator; `elements`, `branches` and `generators` are then unused.

rating.description: The rating loadings are measured against after an outage.

report_existing.description:
Report every branch, interface and bus outside its limits after the
outage, also those that already were before it and got no worse.

skip_zero_impedance.description:
Leave out zero-impedance lines: lines with no resistance and a
reactance at or below `zero_impedance_pu`, as PSS/E treats them
(THRSHZ). Applies to N-1 and N-2, also to listed single elements;
a bus outage still opens them.

worse_by_pct.description:
How many percentage points of loading a branch or interface already
over its limit before the outage must gain to be reported. 1 by
default.

worse_by_pu.description:
How many per unit a bus already outside its voltage limits before
the outage must move further out to be reported. 0.001 by default.

zero_impedance_pu.description:
The zero-impedance threshold in per unit; 0.0001 by default, as
PSS/E's THRSHZ.

cancelled.description: Stopped early: outages after the stop keep their screened result.

categories.description:
Planning event runs: outages and problems in each category, in
category order. Empty in an N-1 run.

monitored.description: Whether a lists file's monitors chose what was checked.

notes.description: Lists file runs: what was skipped and why, in sentences.

rating.description:
The ratings loadings were measured against, after outages and in
the base case.

total.description:
Outages run, and in-service checks skipped because the element was
already out.

with_interface_problems.description: Outages that take a monitored interface over its limit.

case_substations.description: Substations in the case's own data with a place and buses.

estimated_from.description:

reactance where the case gives no lengths) or "neighbours" (at the
average of placed neighbours, with too few placed lines to scale).

from_case.description: Buses placed by the case's own substation data (and not by the file).

from_file.description: Buses of the case placed by the file.

missing.description: Buses with no place at all (no placed bus in their island).

q_mvar.description: MVAr absorbed at the AC bus.

(inverter) bus.

pt.description: MW delivered to the AC system at the receiving end.

qf.description: MVAr injected into the AC system at each end (negative = absorbed).

vsc_detail.description: Converter operating point from the detailed VSC model.

How two-terminal (LCC), VSC and multi-terminal DC lines are solved when
the case has their data.

oneOf.description: MATPOWER's lossless generator pair.
Converter equations with losses, firing angles and taps.

Scale each load's Mvar by the same factor as its MW, so its power
factor stays the same. `mvar` is then ignored.

Also scale non-conforming loads (RAW SCALE = 0), which PSS/E's SCAL
leaves alone: loads that don't follow the system's load level, such
as industrial or station service load.

Reactive power: left out, Mvar stays as it is, unless
`constant_power_factor` moves it with the MW.

mw.description: Real power: left out, MW stays as it is.

mismatch tolerance, so they reach the same answer at different speeds.

load increase in the sink is picked up by all generation.

source_scaling.description: How the source shares out its part: generation by default.

step_mw.description:
The transfer added at each step, MW. 5% of what the sink starts with
(its load, or generation) when absent.

vmin_pu.description:
Low voltage limit for every monitored bus, p.u. Each bus's own
normal low limit from the case when absent (0.9 p.u. when it has
none).

monitored.description:
Monitored buses, and how many of them start below their low limit
(left out of `voltage_limit_mw`).

nose_mw.description:
The largest transfer that converged, MW: the nose when the curve
stopped because the network couldn't carry more.

notes.description: Things worth knowing about the setup, in words.

resolution_mw.description:
The nose lies between `nose_mw` and `nose_mw` plus this, MW (the
last step that failed); 0 when the curve didn't stop at a nose.

solves.description: Steps solved, and how many of them didn't converge.

source.description: What the source and sink could move, as for transfer limits.

voltage_limit_mw.description:
The transfer at which a monitored bus first falls below its low
voltage limit, MW; `None` when none does before the curve stops.

weakest_bus.description: The bus whose voltage falls fastest at the last step.

Rating.description: Which of a branch's three ratings a loading is measured against.

oneOf.description: Rate A (RAW RATE1): normal, long-term.
Rate B (RAW RATE2): short-term, often the post-contingency rating.
Rate C (RAW RATE3): emergency.

RawExport.description: What an export wrote, and what it couldn't keep.

notes.description:
What changed on the way, such as fields the revision has no place
for. Empty when the file holds everything the case had.

source.description:
"records" when the file's own records were written, "model" when the
power flow model was (MATPOWER cases, other RAW revisions).

editable.description: Whether cells can be edited at all (RAW 33/35 and MATPOWER files).

note.description: Shown above every table, such as why the model is shown instead.

revision.description: RAW revision, when read from the file.

editable.description: Whether its cells can be edited (key fields and case details can't).

RecordEdit.description: One cell's new value, as typed.

RecordPage.description: A page of one record type: its columns, and the rows asked for.

RecordRowColumns.description: RecordRow rows as columns: one array per field, each `count` long.

items.description: One value per column: a number, text, or null when absent.
Shared element id (see `crate::elements`), when the record is one.
Line in the file where the record starts (0 when not from the file).

oneOf.description: The RAW file's own records.
The power flow model (MATPOWER columns).

id.description: Stable id, such as "BUS" for RAW or "bus" for the model.

note.description: Why some records are missing, or how to read the table.

rows.description: Sent as columns, like every big table.

skipped.description: Records in the file that couldn't be read into this table.

element.description: Shared element id of the bus or branch, for drawing on the diagram.

index.description: Original row (state row or branch index), for stable "input order" sorting.

rows.description: Rows written: one per finding, plus one per outage with none.

Rule.description:
One filter rule: a field compared with a value. The same rules as the
app's filter chips (`src/lib/filters.ts`).

RunReport.description: What running a run file did.

outcomes.description: Steps that ran, in order (the ones after a failure or a cancel don't).

buses.description: How many buses it has, counting the star bus of a three-winding transformer.

has_coordinates.description: Whether it comes with bus coordinates for the map.

oneOf.description: The total the scaled loads or generators should come to.
Add this much to the total (negative lowers it).

Change by this percent (10 raises it by a tenth). For loads, each
load that scales changes by this much; loads left alone (negative,
non-conforming) don't count.

ScaleLoadParts.description: Which parts of a load scale.

oneOf.description: Constant power, current and admittance parts alike.
Only the constant power part (PL/QL).

ScaleParticipation.description: How a generation change is shared between units.

oneOf.description:
In proportion to each unit's output: every unit scales by the same
factor.
In proportion to each unit's maximum output.

In proportion to each unit's room to move: Pmax - PG going up,
PG - Pmin going down.

ScaleReport.description: What scaling did, or would do.

at_limit.description: How many generators ended at Pmin or Pmax.

buses.description: How many buses the filters chose.

changed.description: How many loads and generators changed in all.

notes.description: Anything worth knowing, such as loads left alone.

rows.description: The biggest changes first, at most [`ROWS_KEPT`] of them.

shortfall_mw.description: Generation MW the units couldn't take within their limits.

buses.description: The buses whose loads and generators scale.

count.description: How many loads or in-service generators are at the chosen buses.

Scaled.description: What `scale_load_generation` answers: what changed, and the case after.

at_limit.description: A generator stopped at Pmin or Pmax.

Scaling.description: How the source and sink share out the transfer.

oneOf.description: Online generators, in proportion to their output now.

Online generators, in proportion to the room they have: up to Pmax
in the source, down to Pmin in the sink. Every unit reaches its
limit at the same transfer.

Loads, in proportion to their MW: the source's loads drop and the
sink's grow.

SectionInfo.description: One record type in the list, without its rows.

area_interchange.description: The area interchange control the solve used (off for DC).

areas.description:
Every area's net interchange (AC only): areas from the case's area
data first, then the others found on buses.

buses.description: Sent as columns (see [`Table`]); the frontend turns them back into rows.

dc_systems.description: DC networks of the multi-terminal systems (detailed model).

dc_tap_passes.description: Passes that stepped DC converter taps (detailed model).

decoupled_iterations.description: How many of `iterations` were decoupled iterations.

facts.description: FACTS devices in service, in file order (RAW only).

interchange_passes.description: Passes that moved area slack generation.

iterations.description: Iterations in all passes, Newton and decoupled together.

newton_fallbacks.description: Passes in which the automatic method finished with Newton.

phase_shifters.description: Phase shifters in active power flow control in the case.

phase_shifters_locked.description: Whether the solve locked the phase shifters at their angles (AC only).

phase_shifters_moved.description: Phase shifters that ended away from their starting angle.

shunts_locked.description:
Whether the solve locked the switched shunts, and the transformer
taps, where they were instead of moving them (AC only).

shunts_switched.description: Switched shunts that ended away from their starting susceptance.

taps_moved.description:
Transformer taps that ended away from their starting ratio, in
voltage control (COD 1), reactive flow control (COD 2) or moved by a
DC line converter (COD 4, with the DC converter taps).

voltage_control_passes.description: Passes that switched shunts or stepped transformer taps.

vsc_grids.description:
VSC DC grids from an attached DC grid file, solved in sequence with
the AC network.

vsc_limit_passes.description: Passes that reduced VSC output to converter MVA or current limits.

SolveSettings.description:
How to solve. Fields left out take their defaults: AC with the automatic
method from the last solution, to 2 MVA, with reactive limits held and
every control on.

adjust_dc_taps.description:
Step DC converter taps, and the transformers that some converters
step instead (COD 4); detailed model only.

adjust_phase_shifters.description:
Move phase shifters in active power flow control (AC only). When
false they are locked, like taps.

adjust_transformer_taps.description:
Step transformer taps in voltage control (COD 1) and reactive flow
control (COD 2) (AC only). When false they are locked, like shunts.

area_interchange.description:
Hold each area's net interchange at its desired value with the
area slack generation (AC only; RAW area data). Off by default.

decoupled_iterations.description:
Decoupled iterations per pass (fixed-slope and fast decoupled, and
the decoupled stage of the automatic method).

enforce_q_limits.description:
Hold generators at their reactive limits (and regulate remote buses).
On by default, as real cases are solved in PSS/E and PowerWorld.

switch_shunts.description:
Switch shunts in voltage control (AC only). When false they are
locked: they stay where they are, which is where the last solve left
them when starting from it, and at their case values otherwise.

tolerance_mva.description:
Largest power mismatch allowed at any bus, in MVA. It converts to per
unit on each case's own base at solve time, so the same setting means
the same MW and Mvar on every case.

Source.description: Where the element inspector reads an element from.

oneOf.description: The power flow model (every file power flow reads).
nodal's topology model (RAW revision 35).
The file's own record, field by field (RAW revisions 33 and 35).
The voltages in the case.
1 p.u. at every bus.

Where the last converged AC solve ended, with its controls where they
ended, also after study edits; the case voltages when there is none.

Step.description:
One command of a run file, with its arguments as JSON, named as the
command takes them (camelCase).

line.description: The line it starts on, from 1.

error.description: Why it failed; absent when it worked.

result.description: What it answered, when results were asked for.

StnExport.description: What converting a case to the Stannum format kept or changed.

notes.description: Anything worth knowing: conversions, data kept as RAW lines.

Subsystem.description:
A set of buses, as a `.stnl` subsystem: listed areas, zones, owners and
buses combine as a union (every bus when all are empty), then the kV
filters narrow it.

kv_max.description: Only buses at or below this base voltage, kV.

kv_min.description: Only buses at or above this base voltage, kV.

derived.description: Built from the power flow model (MATPOWER, RAW other than revision 35).

revision.description: RAW revision nodal read, or 0 when built from the power flow model.

TopologyViewWire.description: The topology after a change of options: the case stays as it was.

TransferContingencies.description:
Which outages to study the transfer under. The base case is always
studied too.

elements.description:
Ids to take out, one at a time, as for contingency analysis (ids
joined by "&" go out together). When absent, every in-service
branch and/or generator, as chosen below.

kv_min.description: Only branch outages with a terminal bus at or above this voltage, kV.

skip_zero_impedance.description: Leave out zero-impedance lines (PSS/E THRSHZ, 0.0001 p.u.).

TransferFactor.description: Base case PTDF of one monitored element.

limit_mw.description: Base rating limit, MW; 0 when unrated.

TransferLimit.description:
One limit the transfer runs into: a monitored element, in the base case
or after a contingency.

contingency.description: What is out, "" for the base case.

contingency_name.description:
The contingency's name: a lists file's name, or PSS/E style;
"BASE CASE" for the base case.

factor.description: Distribution factor: PTDF in the base case, OTDF after an outage.

fcitc_mw.description:
The transfer that brings the element to its limit, MW. Negative
when it is already past it in the direction the transfer pushes.

flow_mw.description: Flow before the transfer (after the contingency), MW, from end.

from.description: End buses of a branch; 0 for an interface.

monitored_name.description:
The monitored element named PSS/E style (bus names and numbers,
then the circuit), or the interface's name.

winding.description: 1-3 for a leg of a three-winding transformer.

contingencies.description: Each contingency's lowest limit, lowest first; the base case is "".

factors.description: Base case PTDFs at or above the cutoff, largest first.

limits.description:
Each monitored element's lowest limit over the base case and every
contingency, lowest first.

past_limits.description:
Elements already past their limit before any transfer (where it
pushes them further), each at its worst, lowest FCITC first. Empty
when `include_past_limits` puts them in `limits`.

contingencies.description: Outages to study; `None` studies the base case only.

cutoff.description:
Elements whose distribution factor is below this (as a fraction,
0.05 = 5%) in size don't limit the transfer.

include_past_limits.description:
Let elements already past their limit before any transfer set the
FCITC (negative). Off by default: they are listed apart in
`past_limits`, and the FCITC is the transfer that first takes an
element within its limit past it.

limit_pct.description: Percent of the rating that counts as the limit.

lists.description:
A lists file (`.stnl`). Its contingencies and contingency sets,
when it has any, are the outages studied instead of
`contingencies`; its flow and interface monitors, when it has any,
are what is watched instead of `monitor`.

max_rows.description: The most rows kept in each of the results' lists.

rating.description: Rating after an outage, and in the base case (`base_rating`).

transfer.description:
The lists file's `transfer` record to run: its source, sink,
scaling, cutoff, ratings and limit replace the ones above. The
file's only transfer when absent.

contingencies.description:
Contingencies studied (the base case not counted), and those left
out because they split the network.

fcitc_mw.description:
The first change of total transfer capability from network limits,
MW; `None` when no monitored element reaches the cutoff.

generation_limit_mw.description:
The most the source and sink can move: the smaller of their
available MW.

notes.description: Things worth knowing about the setup, in words.

transfer_limit_mw.description: The transfer limit: the smaller of the two above.

outages.description: Outages with at least one line.

rows.description:
Lines written, one per violation (and one per outage whose AC solve
failed), not counting the header.

VoltageProblem.description: A bus outside its voltage limits after an outage.

VscDetail.description: Operating point of a VSC DC line under the detailed model.

current_ka.description: DC current from the sending to the receiving end, kA.

from_kv.description: DC voltage at the sending and receiving converters, kV.

from_limited.description: Whether each end's MVA or current limit reduced its output.

from_loss_mw.description: Converter losses at each end, MW.

order_scale.description: Fraction of the power order kept after MVA or current limits.

q_min_mvar.description: Reactive range at the operating point; None without limits.

VscGridsReport.description: The sequential AC/DC solve, for the VSC grids tab.

iterations.description: AC/DC iterations, and AC Newton steps over all of them.

last_change_mva.description: Largest converter change in the last iteration, MVA.

element.description:
The branch or generator whose record the warning is about, as a
shared element id, when the line is one of theirs.

apply_record_edits.doc: Write cell edits into the case and reopen it in place.

bus_coordinates.doc:
Where every bus goes on the map, as columns in bus order, with the
source of each place ("file", "estimated" or "none").

adjust_dc_taps.description:
Step DC converter taps, and the transformers that some converters
step instead (COD 4); detailed model only.

adjust_phase_shifters.description:
Move phase shifters in active power flow control (AC only). When
false they are locked, like taps.

adjust_transformer_taps.description:
Step transformer taps in voltage control (COD 1) and reactive flow
control (COD 2) (AC only). When false they are locked, like shunts.

area_interchange.description:
Hold each area's net interchange at its desired value with the
area slack generation (AC only; RAW area data). Off by default.

decoupled_iterations.description:
Decoupled iterations per pass (fixed-slope and fast decoupled, and
the decoupled stage of the automatic method).

enforce_q_limits.description:
Hold generators at their reactive limits (and regulate remote buses).
On by default, as real cases are solved in PSS/E and PowerWorld.

switch_shunts.description:
Switch shunts in voltage control (AC only). When false they are
locked: they stay where they are, which is where the last solve left
them when starting from it, and at their case values otherwise.

tolerance_mva.description:
Largest power mismatch allowed at any bus, in MVA. It converts to per
unit on each case's own base at solve time, so the same setting means
the same MW and Mvar on every case.

calculate_sensitivities.doc:
Calculate sensitivities at the solved operating point. Takes the same
settings as `solve_power_flow`, in `settings` or one by one.

cancel_contingencies.doc: Stop the contingency run in progress.

cancel_pv_curve.doc: Stop the PV curve study in progress.

cancel_run_file.doc:
Stop the run file in progress before its next line, and the solve or
contingency run it is waiting on.

cancel_solve.doc: Stop the solve in progress; the case keeps its previous results.

cancel_transfer_limits.doc: Stop the transfer limit study in progress.

case_records.doc: The case's record types and their counts.

case_summary.doc: The open case's summary, or null when none is open.

command_schemas.doc:
Every command's arguments and result, and the error, as JSON Schema
(2020-12), for clients that check calls or generate types.

contingency_detail.doc: One outage's flow and voltage changes, by rank.

contingency_page.doc:
A page of the last run's results, sorted, searched and filtered in
the core. Left unsorted, the rows keep their rank order.

contingency_progress.doc: How far the contingency run in progress has got.

contingency_rows.doc: A page of the last run's ranked results.

contingency_summary.doc: The last contingency run's summary, or null.

diagnostics.doc:
Versions and platform for a problem report, and how many internal
errors there have been. Nothing from the case.

diagram_network.doc: The case as a drawable network, for one-line diagrams.

diff_compare.doc: Compare two RAW files record by record.

diff_compare_working.doc: Compare the case's file with the case as it is being worked on.

diff_record_detail.doc: One record of the last comparison, field by field.

diff_section_records.doc: The last comparison's records of one type.

element_detail.doc: One element's data and limits from the file.

element_kinds.doc:
Every kind of element id: its format, the RAW section and MATPOWER
table it comes from, and where the inspector reads it.

export_contingency_results.doc:
Write the last contingency run to a compact results file (`.stnr`):
an Arrow IPC stream, zstd compressed, one row per finding and one per
outage with none. Opens in pyarrow, polars, pandas and DuckDB.

export_contingency_violations.doc:
Write every violation of the last run to a CSV file, one line each:
branch overloads, bus voltages and interfaces, and a line for each
outage whose AC solve failed.

export_matpower.doc: Write the case, solved or as filed, as a MATPOWER file.

export_raw.doc:
Write the case, with its Records and study edits, as a complete PSS/E
RAW file of revision 33 or 35. The answer lists anything the file
couldn't keep.

export_stn.doc:
Write the case, with its Records and study edits, as a Stannum case
file (format preview): binary when `path` ends in `.stnb`, else text
(`.stn`). The answer lists anything converted or kept as RAW lines.

file_fingerprint.doc: Size, hash and date of a file, so a study can tell whether its case changed.

list_commands.doc: The commands this version answers, and the API version.

lists_subsystems.doc: The subsystem records of a lists file (`.stnl`), as written.

load_coordinates.doc:
Attach a bus coordinates CSV (bus, latitude, longitude, optional
substation) to the case, for the map.

load_dc_grids.doc: Attach a Stannum DC grid file to the case.

open_case.doc: Open a case file (PSS/E RAW or MATPOWER). It replaces the open case.

open_sample.doc:
Write a built-in sample case (and its bus coordinates, if it has
any) into `dir`, or a `stannum-samples` folder in the temp folder,
and open it. It replaces the open case.

planning_event_counts.doc:
How many NERC TPL-001 planning events each category gives on the
open case, before running them with `run_contingencies`. Settings
left out take their defaults: every category Stannum generates, at
100 kV and above.

pv_progress.doc: How far the PV curve study in progress has got: solves so far.

record_fields.doc:
How each column of one record type filters: by number, by text, or
by picking one of its few values.

record_page.doc:
A page of one record type, sorted, searched and filtered in the core
(fields are column positions, "line" and "element").

record_table.doc: Every record of one type, with every field.

record_values.doc:
The distinct values of one column of a record type, sorted, missing
last: the choices its filter offers. At most `limit` (500 when left out).

result_branches.doc:
A page of a result's branches. `busRules` keep the branches with an
end at a bus passing every rule.

result_bus_values.doc:
The distinct values of a bus filter field in a result, sorted,
missing last. At most `limit` (500 when left out).

result_buses.doc:
A page of a result's buses, sorted, searched and filtered in the
core. `name` is a result name, or "latest" for the latest solve. `busRules` keep the buses passing every rule (the Power flow
filter chips: area, base_kv, kind, number, name, vm).

result_generators.doc:
A page of a result's generators. `busRules` keep the generators at a
bus passing every rule.

result_report.doc:
A result by name ("base", "study", "contingency 3", "trip line:1:2:1"),
as a full solve report.

run_contingencies.doc:
Run N-1 contingencies, or with `settings.planning` the NERC TPL-001
planning events. `cancel_contingencies` stops the run and
`contingency_progress` follows it. Settings left out take their
defaults: every branch and generator, screened, then the worst in AC.

run_file.doc:
Run a run file (`.stnrun`): commands one per line, in order (see
`run_file`). Every line is checked first. The run stops at the first
command that fails unless `keepGoing`; `results` keeps each answer.

run_file_text.doc:
Commands as run file text, for copying from the app's history.
Paths stay as given and settings at their defaults are left out.

run_pv_curve.doc:
PV curve (continuation power flow): grows a transfer, or the sink's
load, step by step with full AC solves from the last AC solve until
the network can't carry more (the nose), and records the monitored
bus voltages on the way. `cancel_pv_curve` stops it and
`pv_progress` counts its solves.

run_transfer_limits.doc:
Transfer limits (DFAX and FCITC): how much power can move from the
source subsystem to the sink before a monitored branch or interface
reaches its limit, in the base case and after each contingency.
Linear factors on top of the AC solve. `cancel_transfer_limits` stops
the study and `transfer_progress` follows it.

sample_cases.doc: The small cases built into Stannum, to open with `open_sample`.

save_case_as.doc: Save the case, with its edits, to a new file.

save_run_file.doc:
Write commands as a run file, such as ones from the app's history. Paths in
the run file's folder are written relative to it, and settings at
their defaults are left out.

scale_load_generation.doc:
Scale load and generation at a set of buses (areas, zones, owners,
buses and a kV range) to a target total or by a change in MW or
percent, and write the new values into the case's records.

scale_preview.doc: What `scale_load_generation` would change, without changing anything.

sensitivity_responses.doc: One sensitivity column's responses at every bus.

set_study_edits.doc: Replace the study's edits; every later solve uses them.

step instead (COD 4); detailed model only.

false they are locked, like taps.

adjust_transformer_taps.description:
Step transformer taps in voltage control (COD 1) and reactive flow
control (COD 2) (AC only). When false they are locked, like shunts.

area slack generation (AC only; RAW area data). Off by default.

solve_power_flow.doc:
Solve the power flow with the study's edits. `cancel_solve` stops it.
Settings go in `settings` or one by one beside it (`method`,
`tolerance_mva`, `start`, `enforce_q_limits`, `switch_shunts`, ...);
settings left out take their defaults.

study_edits.doc: The study's edits, as `set_study_edits` last set them.

study_locate_case.doc: Where a study's case is now (see `study_file::locate_case`).

study_relative_path.doc: A case's path relative to a study file's folder, if there is one.

topology_set_merge.doc:
Merge buses joined by zero-impedance lines, or split them again. The
answer is the new analysis and graph in the same form as `topology_snapshot`.

topology_shortest_path.doc: The shortest path between two buses, or null.

topology_snapshot.doc:
Islands, bridges and articulation buses, with the case's graph, as
compact columns (see `topology_wire`). Source fields are left out:
`topology_source` sends one element's.

topology_source.doc: The record an element was read from: its fields and RAW lines, or null.

transfer_progress.doc: How far the transfer limit study in progress has got.

trip_and_compare.doc:
Take one element out of the last AC solve and solve again. Loadings
are measured against `rating` after the trip and `base_rating`
before it (both rate A when left out).
